=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/commands/claude-issue-dispatch.md: the launch prompt body (the paragraph replacing the previous `/implement-issue-claude <url>` invocation, in particular the parenthetical `(`issue not started (label check failed; blocker comment not posted)` when the label or the comment call failed)`) | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The failure-branch reply uses one suffix for any of three distinguishable outcomes (label add failed; comment post failed; both failed). When only the `ai:claude-blocked` label POST fails but the comment POST succeeds, the reply says "blocker comment not posted" even though the `<!-- ai:claude-blocked:v1 -->` comment is visible on the issue. Conversely, when the label POST succeeds and the comment POST fails, the same suffix is correct — so the wording is right in only one of three cases. The label-add-failure case is reported inaccurately.
  WHY: The reply is the pickup's only signal that a dispatched start was blocked. The pickup wakes hourly, grep-picks `blocker comment not posted` to triage stuck issues, and would conclude a comment was missing when in fact only the label was missing — leading to needless operator re-runs (`/reclarify`) that re-create the failure, and to missing operator notice that the label add failed (which is the actual state mutation that gates the next `/reclarify`). The same string is duplicated in `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/claude-issue-dispatch.md` and applies equally to the consumer rollout window.
- tests/test_implement_issue_claude_command.py::test_dispatched_session_stops_when_the_claim_was_removed | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The test only asserts the literal presence of `blocker comment not posted` and the relative order of the four branches; it does not exercise the failure-path behavior per call.
  WHY: Without a regression test, future edits to this prompt can silently regress the per-call attribution, and the only detector is a downstream reviewer reading the same prompt string. The pickup's hourly triage relies on a precise string in the session reply to distinguish label-add failure from comment-post failure.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

When only the label add fails and the comment succeeds, the reply claims the comment was not posted even though it is visible on the issue.
  WHY: The session reports an inaccurate state to the pickup's wake report and to operators investigating stuck issues. A target whose label never made it but whose marker comment is visible will be reported as "comment not posted", creating false positives in triage.

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- .claude/commands/claude-issue-dispatch.md (and workflow-templates/.claude/commands/claude-issue-dispatch.md): line 46, parenthetical `(`issue not started (label check failed; blocker comment not posted)` when the label or the comment call failed)` | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The failure-branch reply uses one string for two independent failure modes. The label add and the comment POST are separate REST calls; when the label add fails but the comment succeeds, the session reports `blocker comment not posted` even though the `<!-- ai:claude-blocked:v1 -->` comment is visible on the issue, and it does not signal that the `ai:claude-blocked` label is missing. The reverse case (comment failed, label added) is also conflated.
  WHY: An operator or the pickup's wake report greps `blocker comment not posted`, finds the marker comment visible on the issue, and concludes the report was wrong, eroding trust in the failure path. The missing-label state is not surfaced, so the issue can retain `ai:claude` without `ai:claude-blocked` and appear in-progress to label-based monitors.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
